decision: started an approval's expiry when the request becomes the head of the queue, not when it is enqueued; arming happens only on promotion to the head, and every removal (resolve, deny, denyAll, denyRob, allowDuplicates, or an expiry) arms the new head if one exists, with denyAll/denyRob clearing the armed timer
why: the client shows only the first request, so a queued approval is invisible and could be auto-denied while the user worked on the first
evidence: src/rob/approvals.ts; test/rob/approvals.test.ts
result: only the head expires at its deadline; the queued request survives the head's deadline and expires on its own later deadline, with the deny reason naming the timeout; the external API, default timeout, and injectable scheduler are unchanged

decision: serialized every read-modify-write of one bot's record on a per-bot promise chain inside the store instance, so commit and saveMemory and their concurrent callers cannot interleave
why: commit and saveMemory were two unlocked read-modify-writes of the same file, and the e2e's own 3000ms wake makes that concurrency routine; one commit could be clobbered by a memory edit
evidence: src/bot/store.ts; test/bot/store.test.ts
result: a concurrent commit and saveMemory leave both effects on disk; two processes on one data root remain unsafe by design, with no cross-process locking attempted

evidence: src/serve/team.ts, src/serve/server.ts, src/serve/hub.ts; test/serve/team.test.ts, test/serve/bot-routes-http.test.ts
